### How to Set Up a Promoted Listing on eBay UK (Target Cost‑Per‑Sale 2.5 %)

**Quick tip** – eBay’s cost‑per‑sale target is called **“Promoted Listing Cost‑Per‑Sale”** (LPS).  
You can set it at 2.50 pounds (or the equivalent in whatever currency you set).  
Below is a step‑by‑step guide, including screenshots you should look for, to get your first promoted listing up and running on a mobile phone (Claude app) and on the desktop web interface (if you prefer).

---

## 1. Make Sure You’re Eligible

| Requirement | What to check |
|-------------|---------------|
| **Seller Level** | Gold or higher |  
| **Account Status** | Active, all payments cleared, no de‑liabilities |  
| **Listing Type** | For in‑stock, single‑item listings (no “Store Inventory” or “Collection”) |  
| **Item Category** | Category that allows promoted listings (most categories do) |  

If you’re unsure, go to **My eBay → Seller Hub → Fees & Promotions** – or **"Promoted Listings"** in the mobile app. If it’s disabled, contact eBay support.

---

## 2. Pick the Item

1. **Create or edit a listing** (or click “Promote” next to an existing listing in Seller Hub).  
2. Make sure the listing meets all of eBay’s size, weight, and description guidelines.  
3. Note the **“Sale Price”** – this will be the base price for the LPS campaign.

---

## 3. Set a Cost‑Per‑Sale Target of 2.5 pounds

> **Important**: eBay compares your target to the **average** sale price of similar listings in the same category, *not* the exact listing price.  
> If you set a very low target (e.g., 2 pounds) and your item sells for £10, eBay will still charge you the full 2 × the average sale price, not 2 pounds.

**Procedure (mobile app & web)**

| Step | Mobile App (Claude app) | Desktop Web (My eBay) |
|------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Open the listing** | Tap *“My eBay” → “Selling” → The listing → “Promote”** | Click **Promotions → New Promoted Listing** |
| **Choose “Cost‑per‑sale”** | You’ll see options like “Cost‑per‑in‑view”, “Cost‑per‑sale”. Tap on **“Cost‑per‑sale”**. | Same caption. |
| **Enter target cost** | In the **“Targeted Cost per Sale”** field, type **2.50**. | Same field. |
| **Select currency** | Bottom right, make sure it’s set to **GBP (£)**. | Same. |
| **Save** | Hit **“Save”** or **“Proceed”**. | Click **“Launch”**. |
| **Verify** | A banner will show your target and the expected spend‑rate. | In the dashboard you see “Target: £2.50 per sale”. |

---

## 4. Set a Budget (Optional but Recommended)

If you’re cautious with spending:

| How to set an automatic budget |
|-------------------------------|
| *Click “Set daily/monthly budget”* |  
| *Enter your daily cap* |  
| eBay will stop promoting after you hit the cap. |

Budgeting is done **outside** of the cost‑per‑sale target. It only limits how many impressions you’ll pay for in a day or month.

---

## 5. Monitor & Adjust

| Tool | What to look for |
|------|--------------------|
| **Promoted Listing Dashboard** | *Performance Score* (S‑score), *Spend*, *Impressions*, *Clicks*, *Orders* |
| **Seller Hub → Sales → Promoted Listings** | *Cost per Sale*, *Sales volume* |
| **Analytics → Viewer‑Data** | How many people saw, added to cart, bought |

If you notice the average cost per sale is far higher than £2.50, eBay automatically raises the bid.  
If you’re stuck on a coupon, you can click **“Adjust bid”** or change the target to a higher/lower value.

---

## 6. Troubleshooting Common Problems

| Symptom | Likely cause | Quick fix |
|---------|--------------|-----------|
| **Promote button greyed out** | Not eligible (not Gold Tier or no “Promoted Listings” enabled) | Upgrade your seller level or contact eBay support. |
| **No budget limit** | You didn’t set one | Go back to settings and add a cap. |
| **Target appears ignored** | Your item’s price is too high compared to the average | Increase the target slightly (e.g., 3 £) or rename the listing to match typical vendors. |
| **Low visibility** | Too low a bid or many competitors with higher bid | Raise target to 3–4 £ or add more keywords and quality photos. |

---

## 7. Best Practices for a Low Cost‑Per‑Sale (2.5 £)

1. **Target niché categories** – e.g., hyper‑specific T‑shirt designs, limited‑edition drops.  
2. **Use high‑quality images** – helps with conversion.  
3. **Strong keywords** – do a quick keyword research on eBay’s own search bar and include them in the title/description.  
4. **Include all variants** (size, colour) in a single listing to keep the marketing budget consolidated.  
5. **Set a modest budget** (e.g., £50/day) so you don’t overspend if a price war starts.  

---

## 8. FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Can I cancel the promoted listing later?** | Yes – just go to the listing and tap “Stop Promoting”. |
| **Will eBay charge me the target every time?** | You pay the *actual* cost per sale – if your sale price is £12 and average is £5, the cost will be 2 × £5 = £10, *not* £2.50. |
| **Can I bundle promoted listing with a coupon?** | No – it’s a paid promotion. Combine it with a promotional coupon for best results. |

---

### Quick Summary (Mobile)

1. **Publish** the listing → Tap **Promote**.  
2. Select **Cost‑per‑sale**, type **£2.50** → Confirm.  
3. (Optional) **Set budget**.  
4. Keep an eye on the **Dashboard** and **adjust** if needed.

You’re now ready to launch a very cheap-promoted
